full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN-VARIANT.** The model and the dense travelling stripes are well known. I found no source describing the specific lane arrangement you observed.

**1. Model family.** This is the standard 2D Vicsek model: active matter, dry aligning dilute systems, with metric interactions and vectorial noise. It is the setup of Chaté et al. 2008 and the "liquid-gas / microphase separation" literature. The continuous-time variant is the same class. The "sine alignment plus Gaussian noise" version corresponds to the noisy-Kuramoto-type continuous-time form of the model.

**2. Searches and what they show.**
- **Dense bands in the coexistence region.** This is well documented. Chaté, Ginelli, Grégoire and Raynaud (Phys. Rev. E 77, 046113, 2008) found the onset of collective motion to be discontinuous. They also found that well-defined high-density, high-order propagating solitary structures dominate the dynamics over a large part of parameter space, including the transition region. I checked title, authors, year and venue on PubMed, ADS and CORE. This is the earliest clear source I found.
- **Microphase separation.** Solon, Chaté and Tailleur, PRL 114, 068101 (2015), "From phase to microphase separation in flocking models: the essential role of nonequilibrium fluctuations". I verified the citation only from reference lists in other papers, and I did not read the paper itself. A student review of the Vicsek model summarizes the result: multiple ordered high-density (liquid) bands appear, rather than a single liquid domain coexisting with the gas. The same review says the number of bands grows with the excess density (ρ0 − ρgas), which sets the band number. A later paper adds that giant density fluctuations break large liquid domains and prevent the bands from coarsening further.
- **Review.** Chaté, "Dry Aligning Dilute Active Matter", Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys. 11:189–212 (2020). I verified the citation. Its abstract says generic phase separation occurs, with a coexistence phase involving inhomogeneous nonlinear structures.
- **Opposite-travelling bands or lanes.**
  - In the single-species Vicsek model I found no description of side-by-side lanes of band trains travelling in opposite directions, or of their persistence.
  - Opposite-moving bands appear only in the two-species Vicsek model. Chatterjee, Mangeat et al. 2022 report an antiparallel flocking state where species A and B bands move in opposite directions. There the opposition comes from explicit inter-species anti-alignment, so it is a different mechanism.
  - A recent preprint (Zenodo, about 24 days old) studies lane formation in a Vicsek-type model with bidirectional desired orientation. It says the lane phase is absent in the standard Vicsek model. That differs from your system, which has no built-in bidirectional drive.
  - The discretized Vicsek model paper (New J. Phys., 2024) shows microphase separation with multiple bands moving parallel, or in a cross-sea pattern. That is a related pattern, but it does not describe antiparallel lanes.
  - The Chatterjee-Mangeat paper refers to longitudinal bands or lanes observed in other flocking models. I could not tell which models those are.

**3. What differs, and whether it matters.**
- **Known:** dense travelling stripes at noise 0.28–0.35, their number scaling with system size, and their resistance to coarsening.
- **Not found:** a long-lived, multi-lane arrangement in which neighbouring lanes carry bands moving in opposite directions. Your own numbers give this state a low success rate from random starts (1 of 24).
- **Likely interpretation:** these lanes are probably a long-lived metastable state of the ordinary Vicsek model. Opposite-direction domains are symmetry-allowed, because the zero-net-polarization sector of a periodic box permits them. Their reported lifetime of 10^8 steps may simply reflect how rarely bands in neighbouring lanes reverse or merge. I would treat this as a possible detail of known physics, not a new phenomenon. That is why I say KNOWN-VARIANT and not LITERATURE-SILENT.
- **Searches not done:** I did not look in the Chaté 2008 full text, the Solon 2015 full text, or Kürsten and Ihle's large-scale band papers. Any of them might mention counter-propagating band domains in passing. I ran out of searches before checking.

**4. Confidence: low to medium.** The model identification and the band phenomenology are certain. The "lane" detail rests on search snippets only, and I did not read the main papers in full.
